messages:
alex: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting spike in 502/504s for hosted inference since ~09:30 UTC. Gateway 5xx up ~3x. Seeing memcached/prefix errors in the logs. sample request ids: req-9a1b, req-9a2c. Can SRE triage?

priya: on it. which routes/prefixes are affected? embeddings vs generation? any common customer tags?

alex: mostly /v1/generate endpoints on high token jobs. symptoms: initial timeouts then gateway 502s. logs show memcached connection resets and long wait on KV calls.

ops-bot: [alert] memcached-prefix-prod.* connection_queue_length > 100 (3 clusters) — incident_id=INC-2026-145 

matt: I pulled proxy metrics — connection queue/backlog high on several proxies. quick check: `ss -tan | grep 11211 | wc -l` = ~420 conns on one proxy. also seeing lots of TIME_WAIT/orphan conns.

lina: paste of memcached quick stats:
```
MEMCACHE_STATS: cmds_get: 12e6, get_misses: 8e6, curr_connections: 420, total_connections: 1.2e6, auth_failures: 0
```

high miss rate + connection churn. looks like prefetch fanout behavior for hot prefixes.

matt: hypothesis: prefetch pipeline is opening per-shard connections for large requests -> pool exhaustion -> backend fallthrough -> gateway 5xx. some proxies are hitting connection caps and dropping upstream calls.

priya: mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefetch concurrency for generation routes, 2) temporarily raise memcached pool cap on affected proxy pool, 3) enable per-prefix fallback to origin for highest-impact customers. prefer doing 1+3 immediately.

alex: support will start customer comms. can runtime team push a throttle config now? also need a reproducible repro so support can provide steps to customers.

lina: deploying a conservative change: reduce prefetch concurrency for /v1/generate by 5x and enable prefix fallback for impacted customer prefixes. rolling to 60% of proxies now, ETA ~2m.

ops-bot: [deploy] runtime-config cfg-773 applied to 60% of proxies (started by lina)

matt: metrics update: connection_queue_length trending down, memcached curr_connections dropping, 5xx rate stabilizing on canary proxies. continuing to monitor.

alex: thanks team. I'll update impacted customers and mark escalation. When rollout completes, please post full postmortem notes (root cause, mitigation, follow-ups). :thumbsup:
